Definition: from the same as G3014; scaly, i.e. leprous (a leper):--leper.
BiblicalUsage: leprós means leper — and its range, from the ordinary to the holy, is the point. In Matthew 8:2, "there came a leper and worshipped him"; and in Mark 1:40, "And there came a leper to him". In Luke 17:12, "there met him ten men that were lepers"; and in Luke 4:27, "And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the leper's prayer is the model for mine — Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean — and the ten who stood afar off teach me to come near. I hold that Jesus cleansed the outsider Naaman and the ten and the one, because His mercy is not bound by Israel's borders. My position is that I will not stand afar off; I will come to Him and be cleansed.
RelatedEvents: The Healing of the Ten Lepers
